option_relations.rationale: COVID-19-associated hyperinflammatory myocarditis is a specific cardiac condition, while cytokine release syndrome (CRS) is a systemic inflammatory response. While CRS can contribute to myocarditis, the option is not directly equivalent to or a direct subtype/supertype of CRS.

COVID-19-induced inflammatory cardiac channelopathy with refractory ventricular fibrillation describes a specific cardiac electrical disorder. While inflammation can be part of cytokine release syndrome, this option is not directly equivalent to or a direct subtype/supertype of cytokine release syndrome.

COVID-19-associated cytokine storm is clinically equivalent to cytokine release syndrome, especially when described with cardiac involvement, as cytokine storm is a severe form of cytokine release syndrome.

Channelopathy (e.g., subclinical long QT syndrome) refers to a disorder of ion channels, primarily affecting cardiac electrical activity. This is a distinct pathophysiological process from cytokine release syndrome, although both can lead to cardiac dysfunction.
